summary: Revision 2 extends the revision-1 focus streak on the existing ZestButton without adding a new component or dependency. An optional `sheenTrigger: string | number` joins `focusSheen` on the existing `zest` object (ZestCustomProps), so it flows through the current useZestConfig merge and provider defaultProps. A small private hook (UI/hooks/useSheenTrigger.ts) stores the mount value as a baseline and, on every later change (including a number/string type change), flips a parity flag; the button/wrapper then gains the same three existing marker classes plus a `sheenProgrammatic` marker and an odd/even class. The programmatic sweep reuses the revision-1 gradient, colour variables and `zestFocusSheenSweep` keyframes, but is drawn on each element's still-unused `::before` pseudo-element (regular: the button itself; split: the wrapper, lifted above the two segments) instead of `::after`; because it is a plain class-driven animation and not tied to `:focus-visible` or `:disabled`, it plays on an unfocused, disabled or busy button with no click/state change. Replay needs no timer, forced reflow or extra DOM: each change swaps between two identical keyframe names (`zestFocusSheenSweep` and `zestFocusSheenSweepAlt`), which restarts a finished animation in one render. Whether the sheen is in use now means `focusSheen === true || sheenTrigger !== undefined`; the existing `focusSheen`/`focusSheenSplit` marker classes (and therefore the existing colours and the existing `.focusSheenSplit .dropdownTrigger::before` mount-streak suppression) are applied for that whole set, while a new `sheenFocusOff` marker cancels only the `:focus-visible`/`:has(:focus-visible)` pseudo-element animation when `focusSheen` is false, so a trigger-only button still shows nothing on focus (R1 is preserved) and the programmatic layer is unaffected. Reduced motion is handled entirely in the existing media query, so it follows a live OS change with no JS and no override; the programmatic pseudo-element gets `content: none` there. Cost: one ref and one boolean of state per opted-in button, no listeners, timers, polling, storage or network, no work that grows with the number of buttons or with data, no new dependency and no bundle-size risk beyond a few hundred bytes of CSS/JS; the public exports and existing props are unchanged (additive optional prop only).

touches: UI/ZestButton.tsx (sheenTrigger prop, sheen-in-use marker classes, programmatic/parity classes, no click or disabled/busy gating)
Styles/ZestButton.module.css (programmatic ::before layer, solid/non-solid colours, parity keyframe alias, focus suppression for trigger-only, reduced-motion rule)
__tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheenCharacterization.test.tsx (pin unchanged mount streak and disabled/busy baseline)
documentation and README pages for the new prop

Existing .focusSheen, .focusSheenSplit, sheen<Style>, sheen<Variant> and force-light/force-dark marker classes
Existing .focusSheenSplit .dropdownTrigger::before rule that already suppresses the chevron mount streak
Existing :focus-visible injection and :has(:focus-visible) split focus rule
Existing useZestConfig merge, ZestCustomProps.zest object and split wrapper DOM
Existing prefers-reduced-motion block and jest + CSS-text test helpers

additions.title: Private hook that turns a changing trigger value into one replayable sweep
additions.why: The button needs a tiny piece of state to remember the value it mounted with and to notice each later change without a ref handle or a timer.
acceptance: The hook returns an inactive result for the value present on the first render.
It returns an alternating active result after each later value change, including between 1 and "1".
It returns the same result when the value is set again unchanged, and in React Strict Mode double effects.
It uses no listener, timer or storage and renders once per value change.

additions.title: Restart a finished pseudo-element animation by alternating keyframe names
additions.why: A sweep must genuinely replay on every trigger change, including after the previous sweep ended, without remounting the button or forcing a reflow.
acceptance: Two identical keyframe names exist and the odd/even marker classes reference a different one each time.
Each trigger change swaps the parity class in a single render and a completed sweep visibly restarts.
No timeout, requestAnimationFrame, DOM re-key or extra element is used for replay.

additions.title: Document the programmatic streak everywhere the feature is documented
additions.why: The new option is only usable if people reading the library pages can find what it does, how it differs from focusSheen and how reduced motion affects it.
acceptance: api.md lists sheenTrigger with its string|number type, default (absent) and first-value-on-mount rule.
features.md, examples.md, configuration.md, README.md and the focus-sheen guide show a working sheenTrigger example and state that it works with or without focusSheen.
The pages state that reduced motion disables both triggers and that no prop overrides it.
